conf.description: CISA Protective DNS alert API (dataset=threat-alert, format=api-pull), direct route: JSON-extract the polled/pushed alert record, derive dns.question.name normalization + registered_domain, preserve the raw disposition token on event.action, map threat/rule/host fields to ECS, keep the full record on event.original. Field names are the work order's own explicit PLACEHOLDERS pending confirmation against the real API at onboarding - not invented by this pipeline.

conf.comment: CISA Protective DNS threat-alert, api-pull, direct route. Work order's own warning, verbatim: 'FIELD NAMES BELOW ARE PLACEHOLDERS... nothing about the alert API's record structure is public... every one MUST be confirmed against the agency's Protective DNS User Guide and the API documentation released at onboarding.' This pipeline builds against those given placeholder names (a map-supplied schema, not a guessed one) per recommendations.direct.cribl's instruction to 'build the pipeline to emit full ECS-shaped JSON since no integration exists to parse it later.' Whether collection is REST poll or push webhook is a Source-level decision the work order says must be settled before onboarding; this Pipeline is source-agnostic (operates on whatever JSON lands in _raw) so it works under either.

functions.description: Extract the alert API's JSON body into fields using the work order's placeholder key names

Derive dns.question.name/registered_domain and the threat-enrichment target BEFORE rename (reads original placeholder names); set event.original from _raw; parse alert_time to _time; event.outcome is a documented pipeline constant (every alert record describes a disposition the service actually applied, by analogy with this corpus's userid-dataset convention for the same no-outcome-column situation)
Straight-copy every placeholder field with a direct 1:1 ECS/custom target and no transform
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
